process: lost wax (report.json process and draft.process = "Lost wax"; the lost-wax gates apply, the sand gates do not)
summary: Revise at 6.7 (round 1: 6.3, Caiman: 7, ship bar: 7.5). Every lost-wax gate is green in report.json. I checked finished-metal.stl myself: 1,475,534 triangles, 0 open or non-manifold edges, 0 degenerate faces, and a minimum bore radius of 9.29999 mm. casting-pattern.stl matches it byte for byte apart from the 80-byte header. Round 2 fixed several round-1 faults. The limbs are no longer even tubes. They stand at most 0.75 mm past the cheek (past_cheek_mm 0.748). The toes' thinnest section went from 0.11 to 0.77 mm, with 0.04 mm² under the floor. The ripple band has no visible seams. The tread-like lozenge row on the side faces is gone. The tail now rides the crest shoulder. The Moloch section of the doc now describes the ring as built. Three things hold the ring well below 7.5, and two of them are new. (1) The head is a smooth, bare, pointed wedge. In face.png and face-300 it reads as a star or an arrowhead; in stones.png it reads as a shark's or dolphin's snout. The ball on the snout tip in hero.png reads as a nostril or an eye. The thorny devil's head is small, blunt and thorny. (2) The new hide is 124 granules scattered as separate balls with smooth metal between them. At the nape they cluster like frog spawn or a bunch of grapes, and in hero-300 the dark-ringed balls at the nape still read as eyes. Major cones still stand on round domes with a dark ring at the root (hero.png, mid-body). This is not the close tubercle field punch 4 asked for. (3) The 'sand ripples' now run as vertical wavy lines across the band. They read as wood grain, bark, fur or flames, not as wind-rippled sand. The limbs are now lumpy, beaded shapes with blob feet, with no distinct toes. Lower on the list: the major thorns reach 0.079 mm, while their named treatment promises a 0.28 mm rounded tip. The gate passes as written, but the claim does not match the measurement. One round remains, and the fixes are concrete.
strengths: It still reads as an animal from the outline. In face-300 and hero-300 there is a four-legged, thorned lizard with a horned head and a tapering, whorled tail. The silhouette in side.png is unlike any other Cataphracta ring or Reptilia tile.
The limbs sit where round 1 asked. past_cheek_mm is 0.748, under the 0.8 limit. In face.png every limb drapes onto the cheek instead of sticking out 2-3 mm, so the snag risk is gone.
The toes are now castable: thinnest 0.774 mm, 0.037 mm² under the floor, 'left as cast'. The graver treatment is dropped.
The band texture is continuous. palm.png, side.png and reverse.png show no tile seam, and the tread-like lozenge row on the side faces is gone. The cheeks are polished.
The tail now rides the crest shoulder (shoulder.png, hero.png), not beside the side face, and it keeps its whorled cones. They grade clearly from the nape to the tail tip.

The build is clean at every resolution: coarse, draft and export are watertight with 0 crossings. The field is Castable with a 1.66 mm thinnest wall. The export is 1.48 M triangles, and every land_widths entry is named.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: One subject: a thorny devil on a textured band. The palm (palm.png) carries only the band texture, with no stray motif. The texture's reading is a separate fault (next items).

checklist.item: The hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px, not generic scales or texture
checklist.reason: The ring reads as a spiky lizard only from its outline. The skin between the cones is still mostly bare polished metal, dotted with separate round balls. At the nape the balls clump into a frog-spawn cluster, and in hero-300 they read as eyes. The head is entirely smooth. There is no knobbed, granular devil hide.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines that render crisp, with no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The part's outlines are crisp, and the band seams are gone. The band texture is now soft, vertical wavy grooves across the band. In palm.png and hero-300 it reads as wood grain, fur or flame licks, not wind ripples in sand. The limbs render as melted, beaded lumps (stones.png, reverse.png).

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: No stones by design; 0 previewed, 0 reported. Not applicable.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: Nothing is blocky, but three passages look unresolved rather than sculpted. The head is a plain, smooth, pointed wedge (a shark or dolphin snout in stones.png). The limbs are strings of beads that end in blob paws with no toes. The major cones still sit on round domes ringed by a dark crease (hero.png, mid-body).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: In bare-vs-finished.png, side.png and hero.png the bore-to-side and side-to-crown breaks survive, and the cheeks are polished and flat.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and from the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: This is the only figure-on-band ring in the collection. The tail wraps the shoulder to about -60 deg (side.png). Nothing on the Reptilia sheet resembles it.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large forms (body, tail) and medium forms (cones) read. The small scale is still too sparse: in face.png the head is smooth over about 4 mm, and there are smooth patches of 1.5-2.5 mm between the granules on the flanks. The density is below Caiman's hero, where every surface carries graded detail.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: head and snout (about theta 108-115 deg, the wedge ahead of the nuchal hump)
punch_list.change: Re-sculpt the head as the devil's: short, blunt and rounded, no longer than about 3.5 mm from the nape knob to the snout and about 2.8 mm wide, with no pointed wedge tip. Cover it with the same granule field as the body (0.4-0.6 mm tubercles at about 0.9 mm pitch), plus a row of 3-4 small 0.4 mm cones along each brow ridge behind the two curved brow horns. Remove the ball on the snout tip. Give the head a slight downward tilt so the snout meets the band.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and face-300 the head reads as a blunt, thorned lizard head, not a star, arrowhead or fish snout. The head shows no smooth patch larger than 1.2 mm across. In hero.png nothing on the snout reads as a nostril ball or an eye.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: dorsal and flank hide on the body, nape and upper limbs (theta about 88-170 deg); kind 'granules'
punch_list.change: Replace the 124 separate balls with a close, touching tubercle field. Use polygonal-rounded tubercles 0.5-0.7 mm across and 0.15-0.25 mm high, packed at 0.7-0.9 mm pitch with 0.15-0.2 mm grooves between them (roughly 500-700 in all), so the skin reads as pebbled hide rather than beads on smooth metal. Break up the frog-spawn clump at the nape: the nuchal knob carries the same field plus its two spines. Sink every major-cone root into the field with a 0.3 mm fillet instead of a round dome with a dark crease.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png no bare polished patch on the body, nape or upper limbs is larger than 1.2 mm across. In hero-300 and face-300 no round, dark-ringed ball or cluster at the nape or mid-body reads as an eye, and the body reads as pebbled reptile hide under the cones. land_widths granules stays named, with under_floor_mm2 <= 1.0.

punch_list.zone: Band hide 'Sand ripples' (full circumference, crown only)
punch_list.change: Turn the ripples into sand, not grain. Run the crests mainly around the band (within 20-35 deg of the circumferential direction), not straight across it. Use 1.2-1.6 mm wavelength and 0.2-0.25 mm crest height, with an asymmetric profile: a gentle windward slope and a sharp 0.1 mm lee crest. Let crests fork and end, as dune ripples do, instead of running as parallel wavy lines. Fade the relief to 0 within 1.5 mm of the lizard's outline so the figure stands clear.
punch_list.acceptance: In palm.png and hero-300 the band reads as wind-rippled sand. A viewer does not say wood grain, bark, fur or flames. The crests are sharp-edged at 300 px, and there is no seam anywhere around the band.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: all four limbs and feet (front pair about theta 95-105 deg, rear pair about theta 130-145 deg)
punch_list.change: Smooth the beaded limb outline into one tapering limb, 1.2 mm at the shoulder to 0.8 mm at the wrist, keeping 3-4 small cones on the upper surface. Finish each foot as 5 splayed toes, 0.9-1.2 mm long and 0.8 mm thick at the root, fused flat to the cheek, instead of a blob paw. Keep past_cheek_mm <= 0.8.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png and face.png each limb has a continuous outline with no string of round lumps, and each foot shows 5 distinct toes gripping the band. report.json keeps toes thinnest_mm >= 0.45 and past_cheek_mm <= 0.8.

punch_list.change: Pull the tail fully onto the crest shoulder: its outer edge no more than 0.5 mm past the band edge along its whole length, and its underside fused to the band with a fillet of at least 0.4 mm. In reverse.png it still rides outboard along the cheek edge from about 200 to 250 deg.
punch_list.acceptance: In reverse.png and side.png the tail sits on top of the band everywhere, and nowhere reads as a separate spiked rail beside the side face.

punch_list.zone: report.json land_widths, kind 'major thorns' (thinnest 0.079 mm at 45 deg, r 13.32, z 3.83)
punch_list.change: Make the geometry match the stated treatment: round every major-thorn tip to at least 0.28 mm, as the treatment claims. Alternatively, rewrite the treatment to state the true tip section and how a short-filled point is restored.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json land_widths major thorns thinnest_mm >= 0.25, or the treatment text names the measured tip section.

round1_punch_check.note: The limbs are within the cheek (0.748 mm) and have no ball joints, but they now read as beaded lumps and are not clean, tapering thorned limbs (carried forward as punch 4).

round1_punch_check.status: done on numbers, not on the read
round1_punch_check.note: Toes thinnest 0.774 mm and 0.037 mm² under the floor meet the acceptance numbers, but the feet show blob paws, not 5 distinct toes (punch 4).
The two nape hemispheres are gone. The nape is now a cluster of balls that still reads as eyes in hero-300, and cones still sit on domes mid-body (punch 2).
124 granules were added, but they are sparse beads, and smooth patches well over 1.5 mm remain on the body and the whole head (punches 1 and 2).
No seams and no tread row. The band now reads as wood grain or fur rather than sand (punch 3).
The tail rides the shoulder in hero.png and shoulder.png, but runs outboard in reverse.png (punch 5).
The Moloch section's as-built note names lost wax, the sculpted part and the lost-wax gates.
